title.narrative: Strengthening communities' resilience to wildfires in Chile

description.narrative:
For the past decade, Chile has been experiencing a pressing seasonal emergency due to wildfires in the following regions: Valparaíso, O’Higgins, Maule, Ñuble, Biobío, La Araucanía, Los Ríos y Los Lagos. The Government had declared a State of Constitutional Exception due to Disasters in Biobio, Ñuble and Araucanía regions. In 2026, Wildfires have affected 38,350 hectares from the central and southern areas of Chile affecting biosphere reserves and protected natural areas, urban and rural communities, and critical infrastructure. To this date, 7 schools are closed due to fire and water damage and over 3700 houses burnt to the ground, impacting around 21,000 people.
UNESCO will provide support to the education response of the Ministry of Education of Chile and local authorities, focusing on psychosocial support and socioemotional learning; and by building resilience and foster local communities’ response to wildfires through the participatory development of a set of guidelines tailored to each affected Biosphere Reserve that could guide a community based preventive fire response and initial planning for restauration of affected territories.
